one_line_contribution: A matched-volume decoupled-collection control (grow the bank from memory-OFF episodes) that tries to relocate the cause of self-evolving-memory degradation from what gets written to whether the writing episodes were conditioned on retrieval, crossed 2x2 with a reflective prompt optimizer plus an instruction/bank transplant to test whether the contraction co-adapts into the evolved instruction.
closest_prior_work: The proposal names CoEvo-Mem (2608.01739) and handles it well, but the sharper threat is the model-collapse cluster it cites only as 'formalism.' Alemohammad et al. already establish fresh-data mixing ratio as the knob, which is exactly M50 -- the 'one-line fix' is a transplant, not a discovery. More damaging, the accumulate-vs-replace result (Gerstgrasser et al. 2024) shows recursive degradation is driven by *replacement*, and an append-only memory bank is pure accumulation; that literature therefore predicts the null (A1 ~ A2) unless retrieval competition at k=4 supplies the selection pressure that replacement supplies in the training case. The proposal asserts the transplant 'is not entailed' but never engages the one prior result that specifically predicts its refutation condition. Separately, ExpeL-style pipelines commonly bootstrap insight extraction from unconditioned trajectories, so A2 is closer to existing practice than the framing ('the standard self-evolving loop' = A1) admits; a reviewer may read A1, not A2, as the constructed arm.
strongest_objection: The two arms that carry the paper's practical message are the least powered in the study, and the predictions attached to them are stated below the design's own stated resolution. Measurement says non-core arms (2 seeds) 'support only ~7-8 point contrasts,' yet Prediction 4 demands that B2's tail accuracy sit *within 3 points* of A1 (a 3-point equivalence claim at an 7-8 point MDE -- uncertifiable), and Prediction 5 demands M50 recover 'two-thirds of the A1->A2 tail gap,' i.e. ~4 points of a gap the *core, 3-seed* contrast can only detect at 5-6 points. So 'content gating does not rescue' and 'mixing works' are both unfalsifiable as written, and the headline deployable fix (M50) is a 2-seed arm evaluated once. Compounding this, B2 and B3 break the design's central invariant: the paper claims 'bank size trajectories are identical across arms by construction,' but a verification/self-consistency gate and a coverage gate reject writes by definition. Either they write fewer than 40 items per cycle -- reintroducing the exact bank-size confound F0 exists to control -- or candidates are resampled until 40 pass, which converts both gates into re-rankers with different semantics from the EDV/ConsistencyGate methods they are meant to instantiate. Since B2 is named as 'the most likely way the hypothesis dies,' a competing baseline that is neither size-matched nor faithfully implemented cannot arbitrate anything. Two further defects: (i) metric (b), retrieval-count Gini 'accumulated during collection,' is undefined for A2 and A4, whose collecting episodes have no retrieval at all -- Prediction 2's claim that 'A2 stays flat' is vacuous on that metric; (ii) the mediation analysis regresses instance-level tail correctness on effective rank and cluster coverage, which are bank-level quantities taking one value per arm-seed-cycle and are collinear with arm identity, so 'entering contraction metrics attenuates the deficit by half' is close to guaranteed by construction and is arm-indicator laundering, not mechanism evidence.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Move B2, B3 and M50 to 3 seeds (they are ~4.8k episodes, well inside the stated envelope after cutting the redundant cycle-2 evaluation and the 1,600 null-replicate episodes), or restate Predictions 4 and 5 at the resolution the arms actually support and say so up front. 2) Specify the gate protocol explicitly: resample distillation candidates until 40 pass, report rejection rates, and add a size-matched no-gate control so B2/B3 remain comparable to A1. 3) Redefine the retrieval-concentration metric on the fixed 300-query probe set (a counterfactual retrieval trace computable for every arm) rather than on collection-time retrievals, which do not exist in decoupled arms. 4) Fix the optimizer confound: A4's optimizer evolves instructions against memory-OFF failure traces but is deployed with k=4 memory, so it is optimized under a condition it never sees -- a standard train/deploy mismatch that predicts A4 instructions underperform for reasons unrelated to contraction, and it sits on the wrong side of Prediction 7. Add the missing cell (optimizer evolves on memory-ON episodes over a decoupled-grown bank) to separate bank provenance from the optimizer's evaluation condition. 5) Replace the pooled mediation with within-arm variation (across seeds and cycles, arm fixed) or drop the mediation claim. 6) Report one larger-bank condition (bank growth is cheap; only evaluation is not) so the mechanism is not established solely in a 160-item, k=4 regime chosen because contraction is measurable there.
missing_baseline: An injection-budget arm. The track's own established starting result is that *volume* was the causal lever -- cutting injection from seven items to three eliminated the harm from the same bank -- and this design freezes k=4 at every evaluation in every arm. A contracted bank at fixed k delivers more mutually redundant context than a diverse bank at the same k, so 'narrower support' and 'more redundant injected content' are perfectly confounded, and the single most likely alternative explanation in this literature is untested. A cycle-3 k-sweep (k=1/2/4) on A1 and A2 banks would separate them and costs only evaluation episodes. Also missing, as above, the 2x2's fifth cell: optimizer evolved on memory-conditioned episodes over a decoupled bank, without which A3-vs-A4 is not a clean manipulation of the optimizer channel.
preprint_collision: Above average for this genre and not padded: it names CoEvo-Mem as a near-identical mechanistic premise, refuses to minimize it, explicitly states that a reviewer may read prong 1 as 'testing CoEvo-Mem's premise adversarially,' and pre-commits to a fallback if a decoupled-collection ablation appears in CoEvo-Mem's camera-ready. The admitted gap (no OpenReview 2026 sweep) is the right one to admit, and it is the live risk: the entire novelty case reduces to 'nobody ran the memory-off collection ablation,' which is precisely the shape of a result that lives in a sibling preprint's appendix, and the proposal itself concedes this. Two real deficiencies. First, the collision check treats the model-collapse cluster as supplying only 'formalism' and never searches it for a competing *prediction*; the accumulate-vs-replace line predicts that append-only stores do not collapse, which directly threatens Prediction 1, and the mixing-ratio result already supplies M50. Novelty against that cluster is asserted by the phrase 'transplanting it is not entailed' rather than searched. Second, the check separates every partial collision (Trap of Trajectory, xMemory, DecentMem, EDV, ConsistencyGate) using the same content-vs-policy distinction that the proposal's own refutation condition (iii) concedes may not survive contact with B3 -- if a write-time diversity gate matches A2, the collisions with the retrieval-redundancy and admission-control lines become substantive rather than partial. I found no preprint that already makes this exact claim, but the novelty margin is thinner than the check presents.
